title: Crestline Credit Card Delinquency, Billing Dispute and Closure Figures
content:
These Crestline Credit Card figures govern a past-due account, a billing-error dispute and a closed account's remaining balance.

| Product | Charging suspended after (days past due) | Charge-off at (days past due) | Dispute window after the statement | Longest dispute resolution | Disputed amount left out of the minimum while open | Balance on a closed account |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Auto Care Card Starter | 60 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | repaid under the existing terms, promotional plans continuing |
| Crestline Auto Care Card | 60 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | same |
| Crestline Auto Care Card Preferred | 60 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | same |
| Crestline Auto Care Mastercard | 60 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | same |
| Crestline Auto Care Mastercard Preferred | 60 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | same |
| Crestline Auto Care World Mastercard | 90 | 180 | 60 days | 90 days | Yes | same |

## Definitions

- **Days past due** are counted from the earliest payment due date whose minimum remains unpaid; charging privileges are suspended once that count passes the product's suspension figure.
- **Charge-off:** at 180 days past due the bank closes and charges off the account.
- **Dispute window:** a written billing-error dispute must reach the bank within 60 days after the statement showing the charge; the bank takes at most 90 days to resolve it.

Hypothetical reading: an account 75 days past due is suspended on a Crestline Auto Care Card (figure 60) but not on a Crestline Auto Care World Mastercard (figure 90).
